Could you confirm whether you knew that there were other manoeuvre brigades including -- and I'll name a few you might know them, the 17th Krajina Brigade, the 314 Brigade, and the 303 Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With all the best will in the world it was so long ago that the only thing that sticks in my mind was the 7th Muslimanski Brigade purely because of its title. We never physically saw, I never physically saw the actual manoeuverings taking place but we knew by the nature of the composition of the brigade that it was deployable in more than one location, whereas the majority of the brigades were ground holding brigades as opposed to manoeuvre elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: But did you know that there were other brigades with the same and manoeuvre characteristics as the 7th Brigade within the 3rd Corps area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't honestly say that I knew that directly but assumption was clearly there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Sorry could you just repeat the answer question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't directly say that, yes, I knew but I would assume there was more than one manoeuvre brigade because a brigade in itself can't achieve an impact on the battlefield in that environment on its own.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. You also mentioned that the name Muslim for the brigade was something that drew your attention. Were you aware at the time that there were other brigades within the Bosnian army that were called Muslim brigades providing a place for members of the Muslim faith? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not outside 3 Corps. We didn't receive information from other divisions or locations within Bosnia itself. As I mentioned, all our information went up the chain of command but nothing came down in terms of the rest of the activities of the armies of the HVO or the ABiH elsewhere in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: So you were aware that it was a common usage within the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wasn't aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: All of the statements that you've about the 7th Brigade today, could I just confirm that they are based on a limited amount of information which you had and more on assumptions and rumours at the time? Would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually on the information that we received from the liaison officers on the ground, and again rumours that we obviously heard during the course of meetings of activities, but again we couldn't confirm that they were actually the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Just two questions about the incident in Kacuni on the 25th of January. It's correct that you cannot say which brigade of the 3rd Corps those persons belonged to; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. Very few of the Bosnian units themselves had any distinguishing marks on their uniform denoting their unit insignia. They all tended to have the common Bosnian flag as insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Were you aware at the time, you may not have been, but were you, that there were various brigades of the 3rd Corps operating in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We knew there were, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Lastly, on the document that was shown to you, the mil information summary of the 27th of January, it was shown to you for the purpose of refreshing your memory. I'm not sure whether the Prosecution clearly asked this, but can I confirm that you cannot remember being at that meeting and discussing this particular issue that was referred to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again I can't physically remember if it was at that meeting but the way in which the report is written, it could have been one of the comments that was made in terms of, you know, we have information that suggest X, Y and Z but because there is no comment on the actual report it's not corroborated and that's the problem that we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Looking back now, you can't remember actually being there and discussing that issue; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall that issue being discussed while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: I don't want to take the matter any further then. Suffice to say that is it not right that a single secondhand source as we see there could be wrong, could be confused, could be exaggerated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You mentioned it may be a piece in a jigsaw, but it could be an inaccurate [Realtime transcript read in error "accurate"] piece in the puzzle; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is one correction in the transcript and that's at page 112 line 3. It's not accurate but inaccurate piece in the jigsaw puzzle if that could be corrected, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Lastly, sir, you mentioned that it would be necessary to look at follow-up reports and see what occurred. You were not involved in any such matters, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, unless I was part of a group on the ground who were asked to carry out one of those tasks but in this case I don't recall that being tasked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: We have heard evidence from a Major Guy Chambers who was in the UN command in Kiseljak. He was much later than you in November 1993. He was responsible for receiving military information summaries and summarising them and passing them further along and he received a number of those summaries which were shown to him during the course of his evidence. You of course won't be aware of that, but could you comment on something that he said in his evidence which was that at the end of the day, they had no hard evidence that the Mujahedin element was subordinated to the 7th Muslim Brigade. Would that accord with what you knew at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. We had no hard evidence. We could not physically make the link.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As the Judges have no questions for you, we wish to thank you for making your contribution to the establishment of the truth, and I'm going to ask the usher to accompany you out of the courtroom, but once the blinds have been lowered. Yes? You want to tender the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. If the witness could please sign it and add today's date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could I apologise for speed of my speech at times and I hope it hasn't inconvenienced the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a moment. Mr. Registrar can we have an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it will be admitted as Prosecution Exhibit P943. I see that it has been initialed, so it doesn't have to be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session. The Chamber is going to render two very quick oral decisions. Concerning the request of the Prosecution for admission of three documents into evidence, the Chamber orders that the documents should be admitted with the following note: For the purpose of refreshing the memory and the credibility of the witness. So these are three documents: Milinfosum of the 27th of January, 1993; of the 13th of March, 1993; and the HVO order of the 18th of April, 1993. So this decision is a logical follow-up of a previous decision that we rendered under similar circumstances. That is that these three documents will have a P number, and Mr. Registrar will give us the number, but it will be noted that they were used simply to refresh the memory and credibility of the witness. Can I have three numbers, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The numbers for these exhibits will be: The first Milinfosum of the 27th of January, 1993, P944. The second, dated the 11th of March, 1993, is admitted as P945. And the document dated the 18th of April, 1993, is admitted as P946. The first document has an English version, P44/E [as interpreted], P945/E for the English version -- no, I apologise. The first two documents are in English so they have no other versions, and the last document, P946, does have an English version, so it's P946/E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we wanted you to say that there's this point made that these three documents are being admitted pursuant to the order of the Chamber under the terms that you yourself specified. Now the Chamber is going to render its second decision. Mr. Usher, can you raise the blinds. Concerning the question of translation of the word "odnosno," the Chamber requests that CLSS, through the Registrar, should first -- are you taking a note of this, Mr. Registrar? -- to familiarise themselves with the transcript. Secondly, to familiarise themselves with document P662 in which we come across twice across the word "odnosno," which was translated differently in the original translation in each case, either as "in other words," or with the word "and." Thirdly, the Chamber requests the translation service to explain to us why there were two different translations for the same word. And fourthly, the Chamber requests that the service in question provides with us a new translation, making all the necessary clarifications regarding the word "odnosno," either by reference to dictionaries or any other convenient or appropriate sources. These requests will be specified in a memo which should be addressed to the Chamber and then communicated to all the parties. It is 2.00. I apologise to all those who are required to stay a quarter of an hour longer, but I turn to the Defence to hear about the plan for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Could we go into private session, please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Concerning the previous witness, I didn't ask whether there were any documents to be tendered. No, there aren't. Fine. So it's almost five past two, so I'll see you all again tomorrow at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
